properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued July 22 at 7:27AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
HLSHGX

This product covers Southeast Texas

**A Weakening Tropical Storm Bertha will approach Southeast Texas on
Thursday**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch has been issued for Bolivar Peninsula,
Brazoria Islands, Chambers, Coastal Brazoria, Coastal
Galveston, and Galveston Island

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Bolivar Peninsula,
Brazoria Islands, Chambers, Coastal Brazoria, Coastal
Galveston, and Galveston Island

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 380 miles east of Galveston TX
- 29.5N 88.5W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement West or 270 degrees at 5 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha is currently located off the Mississippi coast
and is expected move westward along the central Gulf Coast through the
next day. Bertha will be moving through an unfavorable environment due
to high wind shear, dry air, and land interaction, so it is expected to
weaken and become even more disorganized. It is forecast to make
landfall along the upper Texas Coast late Thursday morning or early
afternoon as a weak Tropical Storm. No significant impacts to southeast
Texas are expected at this time with the highest probabilities of
tropical storm force winds remaining off the coast and gusts to
tropical storm force winds possible along the immediate coast. Isolated
showers and thunderstorms will be possible through Thursday, but
threat of flooding rain is low.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across coastal
portions of Chambers, Galveston, and Brazoria counties. Potential impacts
in this area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Prepare for locally hazardous surge having possible limited impacts
across Bolivar Peninsula. Potential impacts in this area
include:
- Localized inundation with storm surge flooding mainly along
immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.
- Sections of near-shore roads and parking lots become overspread
with surge water. Driving conditions dangerous in places where
surge water covers the road.
- Moderate beach erosion. Heavy surf also breaching dunes, mainly
in usually vulnerable locations. Strong rip currents.
- Minor to locally moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks,
and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across coastal portions of Southeast Texas. Potential
impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

Elsewhere across Southeast Texas, little to no impact is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Houston/Galveston TX around 10 AM CDT, or sooner if
conditions warrant.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 22 at 4:35AM PDT until July 27 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected. Afternoon temperatures
in the desert valleys will climb into the 108 to 114 degree range,
and may exceed 115 along the Colorado River Valley and 120 in Death
Valley. Overnight lows generally 80 to 95 degrees.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada including the Greater Mojave Desert region.

* WHEN...From 10 AM PDT /10 AM MST/ Thursday to 8 PM PDT /8 PM MST/
Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 22 at 7:26AM EDT until July 22 at 9:30AM EDT by NWS Blacksburg VA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of southwest Virginia, including the following
counties, Smyth and Wythe.

* WHEN...Until 930 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 726 AM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Up
to 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Campbell Creek, Cove Creek, Laurel Run, Hungry Mother Creek,
Lick Creek, Mill Creek, Muskrat Branch, Locust Cove Creek,
Middle Fork Holston River and Monkey Run.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wytheville...                      Rural Retreat...
Marion Wytheville...               Favonia...
Nebo...
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

When it is safe to do so, please send your reports of flooding,
including mudslides or flooded roads, to the National Weather
Service by calling toll free at 1...8 6 6...2 1 5...4 3 2 4. Reports
and pictures can also be shared on the National Weather Service
Blacksburg Facebook page and on X.

properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 22 at 4:05AM MST until July 22 at 9:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Moenkopi Wash in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 900 AM MST /1000 AM MDT/.

* At 405 AM MST /505 AM MDT/, a river gauge on the Moenkopi Wash near
Moenkopi has reported a rise of 11 feet since 1230 AM MST, reaching
major flood stage. This is due to heavy rainfall upstream earlier
Tuesday. Flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding along the Moenkopi Wash.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Moenkopi Wash.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Tuba City and Moenkopi.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 160 between mile markers 318 and 321. U.S. Highway 89 between
mile markers 476 and 478. State Route 264 between mile markers 323
and 324.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Moenkopi Wash, Little Colorado River, Hamblin Wash, Fivemile Wash
and Begashibito Wash.
properties.instruction:
Flooding will continue this morning along the Moenkopi Wash, from
Moenkopi down to the confluence with the Little Colorado River. Roads
and driveways may be washed away in places. If you encounter flood
waters...climb to safety.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:00 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 22 at 3:55AM MST until July 22 at 9:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Agua Fria River in...
Yavapai County in west central Arizona...

* Until 900 AM MST.

* At 355 AM MST, a river gauge on the Agua Fria River just east of
Cordes Lakes reported a rapid rise of 4.5 feet from heavy rain that
occurred upstream Tuesday evening. Flash flooding is already
occurring and will continue southward, possibly reaching Black
Canyon City after 7 AM.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding in and around the Agua
Fria River.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Agua Fria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Black Canyon City and Agua Fria National Monument.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Agua Fria River.
properties.instruction:
Turn Around, Don't Drown! Avoid driving across the Squaw Valley Road
low water crossing in Black Canyon City. Flash flooding of the Agua
Fria is imminent or occurring.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 9:00 AM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 9:00 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.areaDesc: Black Hills and Southwest Interior Lowlands; West Slopes of the Central Cascades Generally above 1500 Feet
properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued July 22 at 3:48AM PDT until July 23 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Red Flag
Warning for lightning and gusty outflow winds which is in effect
from 4 PM PDT this afternoon to 2 PM PDT Thursday. The Fire
Weather Watch is no longer in effect.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 655 Black Hills and
Southwest Interior Lowlands and Fire Weather Zone 659 West
Slopes of the Central Cascades Generally above 1500 Feet.

* WINDS...West 5 to 10 mph except possible gusts 25 to 30 mph
with thunderstorms.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 29 percent.

* LIGHTNING...Isolated thunderstorm coverage is possible across
the southern Cascade Mountains and portions of southwest
Washington. Thunderstorms will develop late Wednesday night and
move from south to north across the area.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Any storms that develop will be capable of
gusty and erratic outflow winds between 25 and 30 miles per
hour. Outflow winds can occur ahead of and behind storms and
cause erratic wind directions.

* TEMPERATURES...High temperatures this afternoon in the 90s. Low
temperatures Thursday morning in the upper 50s to mid 60s.

* TIMING...4 PM PDT this afternoon to 2 PM PDT Thursday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Lightning in dry fuels can cause multiple fire
starts. Thunderstorms can also bring sudden sharp wind shifts on
existing fires, causing rapid changes in a fire's rate of
spread and direction of spread. Thunderstorm outflow winds can
be a threat for several hours following the start of a new
lightning-caused fire. If a fire were to begin, air quality may
diminish in the surrounding area.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either imminent or occurring now. Any fires that develop will
likely spread quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.

* WHERE...Eastern Kitsap County, City of Seattle, Downtown Everett /

Counties, Foothills and Valleys of Snohomish and Northern King

Shoreline / Lynnwood / South Everett Area.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Extreme heat will significantly increase the risk of
heat-related illnesses for much of the population, especially
those who are heat sensitive and those without effective cooling
or adequate hydration.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas immediately along the water will
experience cooler daytime high temperatures.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible.
To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

For sheltering information and other human services in your area,
dial 2 1 1 during business hours or visit wa211.org anytime.

properties.description:
HLSLIX

This product covers Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi

TROPICAL STORM WARNINGS ARE IN PLACE FOR THE CITY OF NEW ORLEANS INCLUDING
ORLEANS, JEFFERSON, ST. CHARLES AND UPPER PLAQUEMINES PARISHES AS WELL
AS LOWER TERREBONNE PARISH.

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Central Jefferson,
Central Plaquemines, Central St. Charles, Coastal Jefferson,
Eastern Orleans, Lower Lafourche, Lower Plaquemines, Lower St.
Bernard, Lower St. Charles, Lower Terrebonne, Southeast St.
Tammany, Southern Hancock, Southern Harrison, Southern Jackson,
Upper Jefferson, Upper Plaquemines, Upper St. Bernard, Upper
St. Charles, and Western Orleans
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Northern Hancock,
Northern Harrison, Northern Jackson, St. John The Baptist,
Upper Lafourche, and Upper Terrebonne

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 120 miles east-southeast of New Orleans LA or about 80
miles southeast of Gulfport MS
- 29.4N 88.3W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement West or 270 degrees at 5 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha is currently south of Mobile Bay and will
continue its westward track moving at 6 mph. Most of its activity is
well into the Gulf, south of southeast Louisiana. It has decreased
slightly in strength since the 10 PM CDT advisory, now has peak winds
at 50 mph, and is expected to continue slowly weakening. Impacts to
the area are expected through early Thursday morning.

Bertha is forecast to bring the threat of tropical storm force wind
gusts to coastal areas of Plaquemines, Jefferson, Lafourche, and
Terrebonne Parishes and locally heavy rainfall generally south of I-
10, and coastal flooding of up to 2 to 4 feet above normally dry
ground. The coastal areas of Mississippi and southeast Louisiana will
have the greatest threat, especially along and south of I-10.

Coastal Flood Warnings are in effect for coastal Mississippi and
Southeast St. Tammany to the Mouth of the Mississippi River. Coastal
Flood Advisories are in effect for north and west shores of Lake
Pontchartrain and the Jefferson/Lafourche Parish Line to Morgan City,
Louisiana.

Tropical Storm Warnings are now in effect for the New Orleans Metro
area as well as Lake Pontchartrain and Lakes Salvador and
Catoaouatche. Along the coast, Tropical Storm Warnings are now in
effect from the Bay/Gulf County Line in Florida border west to Morgan
City, Louisiana. Additionally, Tropical Storm Watches remain in effect
for St. John Parish, inland portions Terrebonne and Lafourche
Parishes, Lake Maurepas, as well as inland portions of coastal
Mississippi Counties of Jackson, Harrison, and Hancock.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* WIND:
Protect against hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
southeast Louisiana and coastal Mississippi. Potential impacts in this
area include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban or
heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on bridges
and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Protect against life-threatening surge having possible significant
impacts across coastal Louisiana and Mississippi. Potential impacts in
this area include:
- Areas of inundation with storm surge flooding accentuated by
waves. Damage to several buildings, mainly near the coast.
- Sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads become
weakened or washed out, especially in usually vulnerable low
spots.
- Major beach erosion with heavy surf breaching dunes. Strong and
numerous rip currents.
- Moderate damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers.
Several small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages.

Elsewhere across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Protect against locally hazardous rainfall flooding having possible
limited impacts across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi.
Potential impacts include:
- Localized rainfall flooding may prompt a few evacuations.
- Rivers and tributaries may quickly rise with swifter currents.
Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may become swollen
and overflow in spots.
- Flood waters can enter a few structures, especially in usually
vulnerable spots. A few places where rapid ponding of water
occurs at underpasses, low-lying spots, and poor drainage
areas. Several storm drains and retention ponds become
near-full and begin to overflow. Some brief road and bridge
closures.

* TORNADOES:
Little to no impacts are anticipated at this time
across Southeast Louisiana and South Mississippi.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to complete all preparations to protect life and
property in accordance with your emergency plan. Ensure you are in a
safe location before the onset of strong winds or possible flooding.

If you are relocating to safe shelter, leave as early as possible.
Allow extra time to reach your destination. Many roads and bridges
will be closed once strong winds arrive. Check the latest weather
forecast before departing and drive with caution.

Failure to adequately shelter may result in serious injury or loss of
life. Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with any
orders that are issued. Remember, during the storm 9 1 1 Emergency
Services may not be able to immediately respond if conditions are
unsafe. This should be a big factor in your decision making.

Keep cell phones well charged. Cell phone chargers for automobiles
can be helpful, but be aware of your risk for deadly carbon monoxide
poisoning if your car is left idling in a garage or other poorly
ventilated area.

It is important to remain calm, informed, and focused during an
emergency. Be patient and helpful with those you encounter.

If you are a visitor, be sure to know the name of the city or town in
which you are staying and the name of the county or parish in which
it resides. Listen for these locations in local news updates. Pay
attention for instructions from local authorities.

Storm surge is the leading killer associated with tropical storms and
hurricanes! Make sure you are in a safe area away from the surge
zone. Even if you are not in a surge-prone area, you could find
yourself cutoff by flood waters during and after the storm. Heed
evacuation orders issued by the local authorities.

Rapidly rising flood waters are deadly. If you are in a flood-prone
area, consider moving to higher ground. Never drive through a flooded
roadway. Remember, turn around don't drown!

If a Tornado Warning is issued for your area, be ready to shelter
quickly, preferably away from windows and in an interior room not
prone to flooding. If driving, scan the roadside for quick shelter
options.

If in a place that is vulnerable to high wind, such as near large
trees, a manufactured home, upper floors of a high-rise building, or
on a boat, consider moving to a safer shelter before the onset of
strong winds or flooding.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather radio or local news outlets
for official storm information. Be ready to adapt to possible changes
to the forecast. Ensure you have multiple ways to receive weather
warnings.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:

- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

Service in New Orleans LA around 10 AM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

WESTWARD**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

- A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for Baldwin Central,

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Bertha is beginning to weaken and will move west of
the local area this morning. Tropical storm force wind gusts of 40 to
50 mph have been observed at times along the immediate coast and
additional tropical storm force gusts along the immediate coast are
possible over the next few hours.

Tide gauges in Pensacola Bay indicate that storm surge inundation of
around 2 ft is occurring, which will result in minor flooding issues
in typically flood prone areas. Similar minor coastal flooding is
possible in coastal Alabama and Mobile Bay this morning. Another round

morning due to the persistent and strong onshore flow in the wake of
Bertha.

rip currents is in effect through Thursday night. A High Surf Warning
remains in effect due to surf of 8 to 11 feet along the Gulf beaches.
These large breaking waves will result in minor beach erosion, along

the Ft. Pickens area, and portions of Highway 399 between Pensacola
Beach and Navarre in the Gulf Islands National Seashore.

coastal Alabama and northwest Florida. Remain well away from locally hazardous
surge having limited impacts.  If realized, these impacts include:

immediate shorelines and in low-lying spots, or in areas
farther inland near where higher surge waters move ashore.

surge water covers the road.

and piers. A few small craft broken away from moorings.

Elsewhere across portions of southwest Alabama...northwest
Florida...south central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.,
little to no impact is anticipated.

* OTHER COASTAL HAZARDS:
Dangerous surf and beach conditions are expected. A high risk of deadly
rip currents continues through much of the week. Surf of 8-11 feet will
continue today.

* WIND:
Potential impacts from the main wind event are now unfolding across
coastal Alabama and northwest Florida. Remain well sheltered from hazardous
wind having possible limited impacts. If realized, these impacts include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.

Elsewhere across portions of southwest Alabama...northwest

little to no impact is anticipated.

**BERTHA MOVING AWAY. TROPICAL STORM WARNINGS ARE CANCELLED.**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 160 miles west-southwest of Panama City
- 29.4N 88.3W
- Storm Intensity 50 mph
- Movement West or 270 degrees at 5 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

...TROPICAL STORM WARNINGS HAVE ENDED AS BERTHA MOVES AWAY FROM THE
REGION...

At 4 AM CDT, the center of Tropical Storm Bertha was located about 165
miles west-southwest of Panama City. Bertha was moving to the west at
5 mph. This general motion away from the region will continue through
Thursday. Maximum sustained winds were near 50 mph.

As Bertha moves further from the eastern Panhandle and in the
direction of Louisiana, weather conditions along the coast will slowly
improve today. Lingering gusty squalls this morning will diminish
around midday. Lingering windy conditions are still expected.
Sustained winds along the coast near 25 mph are expected until this
afternoon, so a Wind Advisory is now in effect for coastal communities
along the Panhandle and Forgotten Coasts.

Ocean and surf conditions will be slower to improve. Very rough surf
will continue into Thursday morning. Substantial improvement in seas
over the open Gulf will finally get underway on Thursday. At the
beaches, life-threatening rip currents will continue through Friday.
Beachgoers should heed the advice of beach flags and plan to have fun
out of the water.

Minor coastal flooding is likely this morning during the high tide
cycle along the coast of Apalachee Bay west of the Aucilla River and
along the Florida Panhandle coast. 1 to 2 feet of inundation over
normally dry ground near the shoreline is expected around the time of
high tide. No additional coastal flooding is expected after the this
morning's high tide cycle.

Brief downpours through today may cause short-lived nuisance flooding
and ponding of water on roads, mainly over the Panhandle.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* SURGE:
Minor coastal flooding remains possible around the time of high tide
this morning along the Panhandle coast and the Forgotten Coast.
Normally dry ground near the shoreline may experience 1 to 2 feet of
inundation.

Elsewhere across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend,
southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* WIND:
Little additional impact is anticipated at this time across eastern
Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend, southeastern Alabama and
southwestern Georgia.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Beachgoers should remain out of the water today due to dangerous surf
conditions.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

As it pertains to this event...this will be the last local statement
issued by the National Weather Service in Tallahassee FL regarding
the effects of tropical cyclone hazards upon the area.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 22 at 3:19AM CDT until July 22 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with heat index values up to 115
expected.

* WHERE...Portions of northeast Louisiana and central, north
central, and northwest Mississippi.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 7 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat and high humidity events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued July 22 at 4:11AM EDT until July 22 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and strong longshore currents in
the surf zone.

* WHERE...The beaches from Cape Hatteras to Surf City.

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT this morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Strong longshore currents will
create dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 9:00 AM Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued July 22 at 1:07AM PDT until July 25 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH IN EFFECT FROM FRIDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH
SATURDAY EVENING FOR STRONG GUSTY WIND AND LOW RH FOR FIRE
WEATHER ZONES 624 AND 625...

The National Weather Service in Medford has issued a Fire Weather
Watch, which is in effect from Friday afternoon through Saturday
evening.

* RED FLAG WARNING AFFECTED AREA...Areas in southern Oregon along
and east of the Cascades, but primarily north and east of a line
from Chiloquin and Sprague River to Lakeview in Fire Weather
Zones 624 and 625.

* THUNDERSTORMS TODAY...Moving roughly north to northeast around
20 mph. Storm mode will be mostly wet thunderstorms, but dry
lightning strikes can occur outside of wet cores. Some of the
stronger storms will contain hail.

* OUTFLOW WINDS...Isolated gusts up to 45 mph.

* FIRE WEATHER WATCH AFFECTED AREA...Nearly all areas east of the
Cascades in Fire Weather Zones 624 and 625.

* WINDS...Southwest to west 10 to 20 mph with gusts 30 to 40 mph
both Friday and Saturday afternoon and evening.

* MINIMUM HUMIDITY...5 to 15 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* DETAILED URL...View the hazard area in detail at
https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. You can find your county's
emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Franklin
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued July 22 at 3:50AM EDT until July 24 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Coastal Franklin County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon EDT today.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even
the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels will remain elevated this
morning. The next high tide will be around 9 am EDT, which is
when the highest water levels are expected along the Franklin
County Coast. During the high tide, 1 to 2 feet of inundation
are expected on normally dry ground near the immediate coast.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kings (Brooklyn), Southwest Suffolk, Southeast
Suffolk, Southern Queens and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Life-threatening rip currents are likely for all
people entering the surf zone. Anyone visiting the beaches
should stay out of the surf. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

you and swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax
and float, and do not swim against the current. If able, swim in
a direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face
the shore and yell or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 22 at 3:23AM EDT until July 22 at 5:08PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in West
Virginia...

Buckhannon River Near Buckhannon affecting Upshur County.

For the Tygart Valley River...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Buckhannon River near Buckhannon.

* WHEN...Until this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 26.0 feet, Major flooding in Buckhannon and
surrounding areas. Business/factory across from the Hall Rd bridge
near the gage begins to flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:45 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 26.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:45 AM EDT Wednesday was 26.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 27.4 feet
this morning. It will then fall below flood stage late this
morning.
- Flood stage is 23.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 27.9
feet on 07/31/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/rlx.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 330 PM EDT.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued July 22 at 12:22AM MST until July 27 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 104 to
115 degrees. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Arizona.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Thursday to 8 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, Call 2-1-1 to find a free
cooling center, transportation, water and more.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

* WHEN...From 11 AM this morning to 8 PM CDT this evening.

extreme heat and high humidity events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

properties.description:

* WHERE...The Big Country, Heartland, and Mason County.

* WHEN...From noon today to 8 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
A Heat Advisory means that hot weather conditions are occurring or
expected. This will create a situation in which heat illnesses are
possible.

Never, ever, leave children or pets alone in enclosed vehicles, not
even for a few minutes. Car interiors can reach lethal temperatures
in a matter of minutes.

Stay indoors and seek air-conditioned buildings. Drink water more
than usual, and avoid dehydrating alcoholic, sugary, or caffeinated
drinks. Dress for the heat by wearing lightweight and light colored
clothing. Eat small meals and eat more often. Monitor those with a
higher vulnerability to heat, including small children. Check in on
family, friends, and neighbors, especially the elderly. If engaging
in outdoor activity, take longer and more frequent breaks and avoid
the hottest parts of the day.

* WHERE...Greater Portland/Vancouver Metro, Western and Central

River and Cowlitz River Valleys, Central Willamette Valley, and

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Smoke from fires outside of the region or
clouds moving into the
area could result in cooler daytime high temperatures than currently
forecast. There is around a 15-25% chance of thunderstorms on
Wednesday afternoon which may increase cloud cover and thus cause
temperatures to be slightly lower than forecast.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in a cool place during the heat of the
day, stay out of the sunshine, and check up on relatives and
neighbors. For those without air conditioning, use fans to keep air
moving. Keeps windows closed during the day and open at night,
unless air quality is degraded due to wildfire smoke.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 22 at 12:09AM CDT until July 22 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Birmingham AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 105 expected.

* WHERE...Bibb, Fayette, Greene, Hale, Jefferson, Lamar, Pickens,
Shelby, Sumter, Tuscaloosa, and Walker Counties.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM CDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stoke. Wear light weight and loose fitting clothing when possible
and drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Harrison, WV
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 22 at 12:08AM EDT until July 23 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Charleston WV
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Charleston has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in West Virginia...

West Fork River above Clarksburg affecting Harrison County.

For the West Fork River...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...West Fork River above Clarksburg.

* WHEN...From early this morning to late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Water begins to enter some homes along the
low sections near the river. Liberty Avenue floods. At 15.0 feet,
Homes along the low sections of the river on Liberty Avenue and
Route 19 flood. At 16.0 feet, Areas of Baltimore Street and River
Road flood. At 18.0 feet, Major flooding occurs along the river in
Clarksburg.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:15 PM EDT Tuesday the stage was 5.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
this morning to a crest of 19.0 feet this morning. It will then
fall below flood stage this evening.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 18.3
feet on 11/20/2003.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/rlx.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 1215 PM EDT.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued July 21 at 8:30PM PDT until July 23 at 9:00PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with temperatures up to 103 degrees. This
will pose a moderate to major risk of heat-related illness.

* WHERE...Eastern Columbia River Gorge of Oregon and Washington,
Lower Columbia Basin of Oregon and Washington, Foothills of the
Northern Blue Mountains of Oregon, Yakima Valley, and Foothills of
the Blue Mountains of Washington.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Wednesday looks to be the hottest day, with
Major HeatRisk across the Columbia Basin, Yakima Valley and
portions of the Gorge and Blue Mountain Foothills.

Thursday will also see widespread moderate HeatRisk and locally
major HeatRisk, mainly across the Columbia Basin.

Smoke from area wildfires could end up affecting how hot
temperatures get.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible.
To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

For sheltering information and other human services in your area,
dial 2 1 1 during business hours or visit 211info.org for Oregon or
wa211.org for Washington anytime.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 21 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Tuesday July 21 to 400 PM Wednesday July 22

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Hot and sunny weather with limited chances
for afternoon storms will allow ozone concentrations to reach the
Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category on Tuesday and Wednesday.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Susitna Valley and Hatcher Pass. This
includes the cities of Skwentna, Willow, Talkeetna, Trapper Creek,
Petersville, and Chulitna.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water
crossings may be flooded. Area rivers, creeks, and streams are
elevated from the previous rain event and will likely rise again
during these next rain events.

- Two additional storm systems will bring rain to the Susitna
Valley, the first Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday morning
and the second Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon.
0.50" to 1" of rain is likely (70-80%) with the first event
with an additional 1.0" to 2.5" of rain likely (70-80%) with
the second event. The track of both systems will favor the
highest rainfall totals over the northern and eastern
Susitna, along the Talkeetna Mountains. As a result, fast
responding rivers and streams along and east of the Parks
Highway may be more susceptible to flooding with this event.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Pinellas, Coastal Hillsborough, Coastal Manatee,
Coastal Sarasota, Coastal Charlotte and Coastal Lee Counties.

* WHEN...through 8 PM Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.areaDesc: Pueblo, CO; Custer, CO
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 21 at 9:10AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Air Quality Health Advisory for Wildfire Smoke.

WHERE...Custer and southwestern Pueblo Counties. Locations
include, but are not limited to Westcliffe, Rye, Beulah, and
Colorado City.

WHEN...900 AM Tuesday July 21 to 900 AM Wednesday July 22

IMPACTS...Moderate to heavy smoke from the Aspen Acres Fire is
possible throughout the advisory area through at least Wednesday
morning.

HEALTH INFORMATION...Public Health Recommendations: If smoke is
thick or becomes thick in your neighborhood you may want to remain
indoors. This is especially true for those with heart disease,
respiratory illnesses, the very young, and older adults. Consider
limiting outdoor activity when moderate to heavy smoke is present.
Consider relocating temporarily if smoke is present indoors and is
making you ill. If visibility is less than 5 miles in smoke in
your neighborhood, smoke has reached levels that are unhealthy.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 20 at 7:40PM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air Quality
Advisory until 4 PM PDT Wednesday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Advisory, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

For additional information...please visit the Web site at
http://www.oregon.gov/DEQ
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 20 at 3:54PM AKDT until July 22 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River.

* WHEN...Until noon AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water could enter a few low-lying cabins along the Yentna River,
particularly near Lake Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 346 PM AKDT, the river gauge on the Yentna River indicates
rises in water levels from heavy rain across the advisory
area. Minor flooding is expected to continue or begin
shortly, especially along the Yentna River near Lake Creek.
- Anticipate water levels along the Yentna River to continue
rising before reaching a crest Tuesday afternoon. Water will
then slowly recede below minor flood levels by around
Wednesday night.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 2:50pm the stage was 20.9 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 22.0 feet is expected around 4:00pm
Tuesday.

Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Anglers Inn & King Point Lodges will have water
in several cabins.

At 22.0 feet: Several lodges and resorts will have water in a
number of cabins with water also encroaching the main lodge
buildings.


For Yentna River near Yentna Station:
At 3:59pm the stage was 18.1 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 21.6 feet is expected around 10:00pm
Tuesday.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- If you live near or along Yentna River, stay alert and be
prepared to take action.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.areaDesc: Jackson, OR
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 20 at 3:16PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air
Pollution Advisory for northern Jackson County...in effect until 2
PM PDT Wednesday.

Wildfires burning in the region combined with forecast conditions
will cause air quality levels to fluctuate and could be at unhealthy
levels.

Smoke levels can change rapidly depending on the weather. People at
risk include infants and young children, people with heart or lung
disease, older adults and pregnant people.

People can take the following precautions to protect their health:

* Follow local burn restrictions to prevent deteriorating air
quality.
* Avoid strenuous outdoor activity during periods of poor air
quality.
* People with heart or lung problems and young children are
especially vulnerable. These people should stay indoors while smoke
levels are high.
* Use certified High Efficiency Particulate Air (HEPA) filters in
indoor heating, ventilation, cooling and air purification systems.

For additional information...please visit the web site at
https://oregonsmoke.org
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.areaDesc: Skagit, WA; Whatcom, WA
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 20 at 12:48PM PDT by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
An Air Quality Alert has been issued by the Northwest Clean Air
Agency until 9 AM PDT Wednesday.

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Skagit and Whatcom Counties,
effective immediately through Wednesday July 22nd at 9am due to
expected wildfire smoke from Canadian wildfires.

Particulate matter (PM2.5) levels may reach Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups. When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, sensitive
groups should take steps to reduce exposure. Limit time outside,
avoid strenuous outdoor activity, and follow tips for cleaner indoor
air. Everyone should watch for symptoms as a sign to reduce exposure.

For current air quality conditions and additional information visit
https://nwcleanairwa.gov
